title: Pork Belly Bao
description: A twist on traditional Italian cuisine, this dish combines the flavors of braised pork belly with the Asian-inspired bao.

ingredients.name: Pork Belly
ingredients.notes: Score the fat in a crisscross pattern

ingredients.name: Caramelized Onions
ingredients.notes: Slow-cooked in a mixture of olive oil and soy sauce

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.notes: Sliced thinly and sautéed in butter

ingredients.name: Star Anise
ingredients.notes: Added to the braise for depth of flavor

ingredients.name: Balsamic Vinegar
ingredients.notes: Used to glaze the pork belly

ingredients.name: Olive Oil
ingredients.notes: Used for cooking the onions and ginger

ingredients.name: Soy Sauce
ingredients.notes: Used to marinate the pork belly

ingredients.name: Hoisin Sauce
ingredients.notes: Used as a glaze for the pork belly

instructions: Score the fat in the pork belly in a crisscross pattern.
Season the pork belly with salt and pepper.
Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear the pork belly until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes per side.
Remove the pork belly from the pot and set aside.
Add 1 tablespoon of butter to the pot and sauté the sliced ginger until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the minced garlic and cook for an additional minute.
Add the sliced onions and cook until caramelized, stirring occasionally.
Add the star anise, soy sauce, and hoisin sauce to the pot and stir to combine.
Return the pork belly to the pot and cover with a lid.
Transfer the pot to the preheated oven and braise for 2 1/2 hours, or until the pork is tender.
Remove the pot from the oven and let the pork belly rest for 10 minutes.
Slice the pork belly into thick slabs and serve on bao buns with caramelized onions and ginger.
